findings.area: SCOPE — these are TWO products on two roadmaps, not one
findings.finding: The A-items split cleanly into (1) CONQUER market-compass report-product fixes anchored to REAL logged user defects — A3 (paid research burns on abandon), A4 (fake-freshness / count!=independence), A5 (report blank/jump) — and (2) generic agent-safety / tooling primitives sourced only from papers + vendor docs with NO logged user incident — A0 (provenance gate), A1 (delete-snapshot hook), A2 (trade-halt indicator). Bundling them as one build is the single biggest framing error the board caught (User Advocate). A3/A4/A5 cite conquer_recording_defects.md (defects c/f/g/h — real pain); A0/A1/A2 cite only arXiv + vendor docs.
findings.evidence: A4/A5 trace to conquer_recording_defects.md (blank/jump 'f', 'Jun26 dates' h, '0-verified' g, stale price-stack c). A0/A1/A2 cite arXiv 2603.20953 / 2511.05524 + Nasdaq RSS docs + code.claude.com checkpointing docs — no user complaint attached.
findings.implication: Phase the work as TWO tracks. Track 1 (CONQUER, ship-now): A3/A4/A5 — user-pain-backed, code-verified. Track 2 (agent-safety R&D, gate behind 'observed in the wild' + a corpus pilot): A0/A1/A2. Do not let agent-safety research block or masquerade as CONQUER user-pain work.

findings.area: CITATION INTEGRITY — papers resolve, but several decorative sub-stats were not in the abstracts and are now removed
findings.finding: The board's worst-case hypothesis (fabricated 2026-dated arXiv IDs) is DISPROVEN: I resolved the load-bearing IDs and the core claims hold. But several precise sub-statistics quoted in the prior draft are NOT in the abstracts and have been struck. KEPT (verified): EviBound 2511.05524 = dual gate (Approval+Verification), run_id/artifacts/FINISHED, 0% hallucination 7/8 verified + 1/8 blocked, ~8.3% overhead, n=8; 2603.20953 'Before the Tool Call' = synchronous pre-action interception + signed audit record, 53ms median N=1,000, 0% attack success across 879 attempts; 2604.03173 = 3-13% of citation URLs hallucinated, 5-18% non-resolving, deep-research agents worse than search-augmented LLMs (over 221k URLs, DRBench+ExpertQA); 2604.04978 'Measuring the Permission Gate' = 81.0% e2e FNR, 36.8% bypass via Tier-2 in-project edits, 92.9% FN on cleanup; InferAct 2407.11843 = up to 20% Macro-F1 gain. STRUCK (not in abstracts / unverifiable): the 'four-layer safety stack' framing, Ed25519, 76ms p99, ALLOW/DENY/ESCALATE attributed to 2603.20953, the 100%->25%->0% verify-only intermediate, the precise 10.7%-vs-4.8% / 16.2%-vs-6.8% / 13.3%-flagship splits (abstract gives RANGES only), and InferAct's '50% fewer interventions / 2 LLM calls'.
findings.evidence: WebFetch of arxiv.org/abs/{2511.05524, 2603.20953, 2604.03173, 2604.04978, 2407.11843} on 2026-06-20; abstracts confirm the KEPT figures and omit the STRUCK ones.
findings.implication: Every external number that survives is now abstract-confirmed; treat any range as a range (3-13%, not 10.7%). The dual-gate architecture and the coverage-bypass thesis stand on resolved evidence; the precise latency/overhead percentages are real but measured on DIFFERENT mechanisms (policy-ACL checks; code-execution artifacts) and must be relabeled as analogical priors, never as A0's predicted operating point.

findings.area: CODE CITATIONS — pin to the market-compass/ tree; board read a stale copy
findings.finding: The board's 'files absent / line-number drift' complaint is an artifact of reading the wrong tree (conquer/ or an older mc_v8 copy). Against market-compass/ EVERY load-bearing code citation matches the quoted lines exactly. Re-verified this session: engine-light.ts:281-292 (demote codomain {single,inferred}), :303-309 (cleanCitations filters valid.has only, slice(0,4), NO domain dedupe), :199 (last_verified:this.today); engine-proxy.ts:118-128 (keyedFetch(service,path,payload) — no signal param, private 28s controller); research-backbone.ts:306 & :325 (two bare Promise.all batches); competitor-verify.ts:398-417 (Promise.race([run(),setTimeout]) — run()'s inner controllers NOT aborted on budget-win); category-regime.ts:571-572 (confidence:'single', citations:[] — the curated-layer contradiction is REAL); report.$reportId.tsx:204-227 (module shownReports Set + lastGoodReports Map + R136 comment).
findings.evidence: Direct Read of all cited files under C:/Users/larsg/OneDrive/Dokumente/Buisiness/Automising my life/market-compass/src/lib/conquer/ and /src/routes/ this session; line numbers matched verbatim.
findings.implication: Pin all code citations to the market-compass/ tree (ideally a commit SHA) so reviewers stop chasing the conquer/ copy. The code-grounded layer of A3/A4/A5 survives adversarial verification intact — these are ship-worthy.

findings.area: A0 — DE-CONFLATE: A0-runtime (report gate) vs A0-agent (tribunal gate) are two machines in two runtimes
findings.finding: The prior draft fused two different components: (A0-runtime) a gate that grades the GENERATED REPORT inside the Cloudflare Worker / SQL layer — this is what engine-light demote() + the fabrication_law CHECK + the _verify CI harness already 80% implement; and (A0-agent) a gate that catches the AGENT's own 'done'/overclaim in a Claude Code tribunal loop — which is NOT built and is NOT analogous to demote(), because demote() runs in a worker and has zero access to the agent's tool stream. 'Generalize demote() into A0' and 'A0 gates every shippable assertion the agent emits' cannot be one component.
findings.evidence: engine-light.ts:281-292 (demote runs in the product runtime, grades report claims); arXiv 2511.05524 (EviBound gates code-execution artifacts, not free-text); Staff-Eng + Claude-Code-expert board defects (runtime category error).
findings.implication: Specify A0-runtime and A0-agent as separate deliverables against their real runtimes. A0-runtime = extend demote() to a pure gradeConfidence() over the provenance object (mostly built). A0-agent = a Claude Code orchestrator-side / hook-level check on what a subagent RETURNS — do not reuse demote() for it.

findings.area: A0-agent — name the enforcement locus; the 'done'/overclaim path is invisible to PreToolUse
findings.finding: A0-agent's headline ('catch the done/overclaim divergence') is not wired to any primitive that fires on that event. A subagent's final natural-language completion message is NOT a tool call, so NO PreToolUse hook ever sees it; and a Task-spawned subagent returns only a single final text result, sharing no tool transcript with the orchestrator — so a peer subagent cannot 'grade another's hidden reasoning,' only its returned artifact. The dual gate therefore has a hole on its primary target unless the completion path is explicitly gated.
findings.evidence: Claude Code docs (PreToolUse fires on tool calls; Stop/SubagentStop fires when the agent finishes and can block with continue:false); Task-subagent isolation (single returned result, no shared transcript); board (Claude-Code expert, high-severity defect).
findings.implication: Specify the enforcement locus per gate: pre-build = deterministic check (hook or orchestrator code) on the provenance object the producing subagent RETURNS; completion/'done' claim = a Stop/SubagentStop hook (or orchestrator-side assertion over the returned result), NOT a PreToolUse hook; post-build = orchestrator-side re-resolve/span-match on the final artifact bytes. State explicitly that no subagent grades another's hidden reasoning — only its returned artifact — closing the 'same model family judges itself' gap.

findings.area: A0 — provenance must be a machine-checkable OBJECT; the agent's own research URLs are the highest-risk input
findings.finding: The admission criterion must be a deterministic artifact (resolvable URL + content hash + char-offset/quote span re-extractable and matched), never the model's narrative that a source exists. Agent-produced deep-research URLs are the worst input: 3-13% of citation URLs across commercial models/deep-research agents are hallucinated and 5-18% non-resolving, with deep-research agents worse than plain search-augmented LLMs. CONQUER's 03-claims.sql already models claim_provenance as char_start/char_end + chunk_sha256 + raw_sha256.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2604.03173 (over 221k URLs, DRBench+ExpertQA; ranges confirmed in abstract); CONQUER 03-claims.sql (claim_provenance shape); validates the CONQUER instinct that 'two sources agreeing' is gameable via echo/syndication.
findings.implication: A0's input contract = {source id + content hash + quote span}; independently resolve and span-match every agent-produced URL before it counts as provenance. Reuse the CONQUER claim_provenance shape as the evidence contract. Treat agent-produced citations as untrusted by default.

findings.area: A0 — gate the ARTIFACT boundary (coverage), not one chokepoint
findings.finding: The dominant real-world failure of pre-action gates is COVERAGE, not classifier accuracy: agents route around the gated path. In a Claude Code auto-mode stress test, 36.8% of state-changing actions bypassed the permission classifier via Tier-2 in-project file edits, yielding an 81.0% end-to-end FNR and 92.9% FN on cleanup tasks. Caveat: this characterizes Claude Code auto-mode in a stress test, a different system from CONQUER — the transferable lesson is the coverage principle, not the specific rate.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2604.04978 'Measuring the Permission Gate' (81.0% FNR 95% CI 73.8-87.4, 36.8% Tier-2 bypass, 92.9% cleanup FN — all abstract-confirmed).
findings.implication: Enumerate the ACTUAL Claude Code exit paths and bind A0-agent to each: Bash (PreToolUse/Bash), Edit/Write/NotebookEdit (PreToolUse with those matchers), MCP calls (mcp__server__tool matcher), and the final assistant message (Stop/SubagentStop — no PreToolUse sees it). A gate on publish-only is theater if an unverified claim exits via an ungated edit or a prose 'done'.

findings.area: A0 — fail-open vs fail-closed is a HYPOTHESIS to A/B-test on the tribunal's own corpus, not an evidence-backed default
findings.finding: The strongest published fail-closed result (EviBound 0% false claims) is n=8 on CODE-EXECUTION artifacts, not free-text research claims; no published eval tests a provenance gate inside a self-critiquing tribunal where the same model family produces and partly judges the claim. The live CONQUER schema chose FAIL-OPEN (demote checkmark->warn + incident), a defensible middle path. Blanket fail-closed carries real over-block cost and breeds 'verification theater' (repeated false alarms -> developers inspect output less) — and for a single-user hands-off tool, a blocking gate is plausibly net-negative for adoption.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2511.05524 (0% is fail-closed, n=8, code artifacts); IBM/UC-Berkeley MAST ('never let the LLM grade its own homework'); over-block cost evidence comes from the tool-authorization domain (different domain — see gaps).
findings.implication: Do NOT ship a global blocking gate as an evidence-backed default. Gate by claim_class as a HYPOTHESIS: fail-closed (BLOCK/ESCALATE) candidate for dynamic/financial/numeric/externally-cited + 'done' assertions; fail-open (demote-and-log, the CONQUER pattern) for static/low-stakes. Before flipping ANY class to fail-closed, run a pilot on the tribunal's OWN corpus, instrument block-rate + FPR from day one, and set the over-block alarm threshold first. Treat the cited percentages as directional priors, not targets.

findings.area: A0 — decision is a recomputed pure function with a deny enum, logged; but 'source-supports-claim' is entailment-scored, not deterministic
findings.finding: The pass/fail must be a deterministic function of the provenance object, never the model's verbalized confidence (systematically overconfident). The decision should emit a 3-valued result + a machine-readable deny enum to the audit ledger. HOWEVER, the most fabrication-prone check — does the source actually SUPPORT the claim — is itself an LLM/NLI judgment; calling it a 'deterministic predicate' smuggles a model back into the trusted path. Only URL-resolves and recency/independence are truly deterministic.
findings.evidence: CONQUER 03-claims.sql (confidence_flag computed via CHECK fabrication_law + BEFORE-INSERT trigger, 'never written by an LLM'); KNOWLEDGE-ENGINE-SPEC sec5 ('never trust raw verbalized LLM confidences'); board (Staff-Eng: entailment is not deterministic).
findings.implication: A0 emits {ALLOW|BLOCK|ESCALATE} + deny-reason enum (provenance.unresolvable, provenance.span_mismatch, provenance.single_cluster, claim.dynamic_unverified) to the CONQUER incidents/audit ledger. Implement the truly-deterministic checks (URL resolves, hash/span match, recency, independence clustering) as code/SQL. Rename the support check honestly: 'entailment-scored, thresholded' — a probabilistic input gated by a deterministic threshold benchmarked on the corpus, NOT a deterministic predicate.

findings.area: A0 — split work by cost: cheap checks sync, expensive checks async; do NOT load the blocking window
findings.finding: The cited 53ms / ~8.3% figures are for CHEAP policy/ACL checks (2603.20953) and code-artifact verification (2511.05524) respectively — NOT for what the tribunal actually needs. The real checks (URL resolution at scale, span-match, NLI/HHEM entailment, MinHash independence clustering, on the agent's OWN deep-research URLs) are seconds-to-minutes and network-bound. A synchronous PreToolUse path blocks the tool for up to its hook timeout; loading it with network/NLI work stalls the agent.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2603.20953 (53ms = cheap policy check); 2511.05524 (8.3% = code-artifact verify); board (Staff-Eng + Claude-Code expert, latency defect).
findings.implication: Hard constraint: cheap deterministic checks (hash/span/URL-resolve) run synchronously in the pre-gate; expensive checks (entailment, independence clustering) run async in the post-build gate or a sampled auditor, never inside the blocking hook window. The phase gate MUST include a measured end-to-end provenance-check latency on the tribunal's own corpus before locking thresholds — without it, A0 is theater.

findings.area: A1 — the delete seam is vendor-conceded (verbatim) and Windows-corroborated
findings.finding: Claude Code file checkpointing explicitly does NOT capture Bash-mediated changes and does NOT undo directory create/move/delete — confirmed verbatim against the live doc. Independently, the issue tracker confirms /rewind advertises a deletion-undo it cannot deliver, reported on Windows + VS Code — directly on-point for A1's dominant irreversible class (deletes) and the user's Windows-first environment.
findings.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing — Warning: 'Changes made through Bash commands (like echo > file.txt or sed -i) are not captured by the checkpoint system'; Limitations: 'Creating, moving, or deleting directories is not undone by rewinding.' GitHub anthropics/claude-code #34368 '[BUG] Rewind offers to undo file deletions it cannot actually restore' (closed not-planned; repro on Windows + VS Code).
findings.implication: A pre-bash snapshot plugs an openly documented hole. Snapshot exactly the bytes Edit/Write checkpointing cannot see (rm/mv/sed -i/redirection/truncate); do not duplicate /rewind's Edit/Write coverage. Cite #34368 as the primary evidence (stronger than the #14002 0-file race because it speaks to deletions and to /rewind over-promising a restore).

findings.area: A1 — synchronous PreToolUse/Bash hook, but DOWNGRADE-not-deadlock and per-shell shapes (Windows-first)
findings.finding: PreToolUse(Bash) receives the exact command string + cwd before execution and can allow/deny/ask/rewrite (600s timeout) — a clean, model-cooperation-free interception point, and hooks are synchronous by default. BUT the same primitive only sees the TOP-LEVEL command string: script-wrapped, glob-expanded, and variable-expanded destructive targets are not statically resolvable, so a fail-CLOSED-on-snapshot-failure rule would DEADLOCK the agent on every command it can't resolve. And the destructive SHAPES (rm, sed -i, find -delete, dd, git reset --hard) plus reflink/hardlink COW are POSIX-specific; the user is Windows-primary where the command is PowerShell (Remove-Item, Set-Content) and reflink is not universally available on NTFS.
findings.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (command+cwd, permission decisions, 600s, synchronous-by-default); destructive_command_guard (scripts-to-disk bypass; fails open); board (Staff-Eng + Claude-Code expert: deadlock + cross-platform).
findings.implication: Make v1 effect-based but DOWNGRADE not deadlock: on unresolvable/script-wrapped targets escalate to 'ask' (never silent fail-open, never hard deny-all). Specify per-shell shape sets (POSIX rm/sed-i/find-delete/dd AND PowerShell Remove-Item/Clear-Content/Set-Content) and a Windows-viable snapshot (copy / VSS), since reflink is ReFS/dev-drive-only on Windows. MEASURE reflink/hardlink/copy latency on the target FS before any 'cheap' claim. Surface the 'NOT captured' classes to the user (mirror Anthropic's own checkpointing warning) and NEVER advertise 'fully reversible'. Treat a staging COW filesystem (YoloFS) as north-star v2.

findings.area: A2 — confirm need + feed schema BEFORE building; freshness is structurally capped at ~60s and may be too slow to matter
findings.finding: The only passive, free, web-only source — Nasdaq Trade Halt RSS — refreshes once per minute and forbids faster polling, so best-achievable halt freshness is ~60s stale, never live; the halt mechanism moves an order of magnitude faster (LULD Limit State -> 5-min pause). Two gating unknowns make A2 premature: (1) it is UNCONFIRMED whether the tool needs intraday halt state at all vs an at-open snapshot — if at-open only, the 60s lag is largely moot; (2) the RSS field schema (machine-readable resumption timestamp/reason/threshold in the body vs HTML-only) is UNCONFIRMED, so it is unknown whether the indicator can even parse resumption. There is also NO logged user request for this feature.
findings.evidence: nasdaqtrader.com TradeHaltRSS ('refreshes once a minute', 'do not query more than once a minute'); SEC/LULD plan (15s->pause); board (User-Advocate: no user-need evidence; Skeptic/Staff-Eng: schema + at-open-vs-intraday unconfirmed).
findings.implication: PARK A2 until (a) a user confirms they want an 'is this name paused?' flag AND that a 60s-stale flag is useful given the mechanism moves ~4x faster, and (b) one live RSS sample is fetched to confirm the field schema. If built: poll exactly once/minute, stamp 'as of HH:MM:SS, up to 60s old', frame as contextual not real-time, never infer halts from the 15-20min-delayed free price feeds (label that delay separately), render resumption as 'expected ~5 min, pending auction + new bands', calibrate any open-time flag to the doubled 9:30-9:45 ET LULD bands, and document the paid-feed ceiling. A feature admittedly too slow to be actionable is friction, not value.

findings.area: A3 — root cause: Promise combinators have no cancellation; backbone fan-out is uncoordinated
findings.finding: runResearchBackbone fans out across two bare Promise.all batches with NO shared AbortController or aggregate budget; JS combinators never abort siblings, so an abandoned report leaves every in-flight Perplexity/Firecrawl call burning its full 28s + paid spend. Blast radius today is bounded (every leaf has a private timeout, passes fail-open) — a cost/robustness defect, not an outage; Priority-4 is right.
findings.evidence: Verified research-backbone.ts:306 & :325 (two unguarded Promise.all, no signal threaded); MDN (Promise.all doesn't cancel in-flight fetches).
findings.implication: Give runResearchBackbone ONE shared AbortController + aggregate budget (setTimeout->ctrl.abort, clearTimeout in finally), thread ctrl.signal into every pass, so a blown budget or abandoned phase cancels in-flight siblings.

findings.area: A3 — the leaf fetch can't receive a parent signal (inert-watchdog); the fix exists elsewhere in the repo
findings.finding: keyedFetch creates its OWN private 28s AbortController and exposes no signal/opts param, so any higher watchdog is inert. verifyCompetitorEntities' wall-clock cap is Promise.race([run(),setTimeout]): when the budget wins, run() and its inner per-fetch controllers are NOT aborted — the 'hard wall' stops AWAITING, not RUNNING. The correct single-call watchdog already exists in callResearchCompany (one controller + signal + finally clearTimeout) — A3 is generalizing it to the fan-out.
findings.evidence: Verified engine-proxy.ts:118-128 (keyedFetch(service,path,payload) — no opts; local controller + 28s timer); competitor-verify.ts:398-417 (Promise.race; inner verifyProduct controllers separate); research-company.ts (correct watchdog pattern).
findings.implication: Thread a signal THROUGH keyedFetch: keyedFetch(service,path,payload,opts?:{signal}) -> fetch with AbortSignal.any([controller.signal, opts.signal].filter(Boolean)). Replace the leaky Promise.race in verifyCompetitorEntities with an AbortController whose abort BOTH wins the wait AND is handed to every verifyProduct fetch. Without the leaf change, every higher watchdog stays inert.

findings.area: A3 — runtime supports the clean fix; do not rely on Cloudflare float-cancel
findings.finding: The SSR runs as a Cloudflare Worker (workerd), where AbortSignal.timeout() and AbortSignal.any() are both supported — the exact primitive to merge a per-call timeout with a shared budget controller. Cloudflare auto-cancels floating promises at invocation end (partial mitigation) but does NOT bound mid-request waste and silently breaks if work moves into ctx.waitUntil(). NOTE: the workerd AbortSignal support date and the Request.signal behavior are framework/runtime claims verified separately from the Claude Code primitives — keep them at 'needs runtime confirmation' rather than bundling at the same confidence as the code-verified leaf bug.
findings.evidence: workerd changelog (AbortSignal.timeout/any); Cloudflare Workers docs (floating-promise + client-disconnect cancellation, enable_request_signal). Verified passes return PassResult rather than throw (fail-open).
findings.implication: Standardize on AbortSignal.any([parentSignal, AbortSignal.timeout(perCallMs)]) for every fan-out leaf; always clearTimeout in finally; do NOT rely on invocation-end float-cancel as the mechanism; optionally wire incoming Request.signal so an abandoned report cancels paid research. Keep proportionate — no p-limit/semaphore/task-runner dependency. Add one test asserting in-flight leaves receive an abort when the aggregate budget fires.

findings.area: A4 — honesty flag mechanism is correct, but checkmark is structurally unreachable at runtime by design
findings.finding: engine-light.ts demote(raw,citeCount) recomputes confidence server-side from surviving-citation count, ignoring the LLM's self-reported flag — the right architecture. But its codomain is exactly {single, inferred}; 'verified' (checkmark) is reserved for human review by design, so the live engine can NEVER emit checkmark. The checkmark/warn/? grammar (confidence-grammar skill, checkmark = two INDEPENDENT Tier-A/B sources) and the runtime engine are intentionally mismatched: the engine has no notion of tiers or independence.
findings.evidence: Verified engine-light.ts:288-291 (signature ': single|inferred'; citeCount===0->inferred), comment :281-287 'groundedness gate (fabrication law, in code)'.
findings.implication: Keep checkmark structurally unreachable at runtime and SAY SO — surface a one-line legend ('checkmark = human-reviewed') so a report of warn/? reads as rigor, not weakness. Generalize demote() into a pure gradeConfidence({validCitations, distinctDomains, sourceAgeMonths, isProjection}) and route BOTH the live and curated layers through it.

findings.area: A4 — count != independence, and last_verified is a fake-freshness leak
findings.finding: cleanCitations counts surviving citation IDs and slices to 4 with NO domain/publisher dedupe (verified engine-light.ts:303-309), so 3 citations to one domain or one re-syndicated wire clear any count threshold — yet checkmark is defined on INDEPENDENCE. Separately, every citation is stamped last_verified=today regardless of the source's real publish date (engine-light.ts:199), manufacturing false freshness — matches logged defects 'Jun26 dates' and '0-verified'. Domain-dedupe logic already exists for competitors in research-company.ts but is not applied to the citation path.
findings.evidence: Verified engine-light.ts:303-309 (valid.has(x) only, slice(0,4), no dedupe), :199 (last_verified:this.today); MEMORY conquer_recording_defects.md (defects g, h).
findings.implication: Count DISTINCT citation DOMAINS not raw IDs (reuse the competitor domain-dedupe) to unlock a deterministically-earned middle rung with no Claude call; stop stamping last_verified=today — parse a real per-source date and drive a staleness signal (downgrade/annotate when freshest source >12-18mo); pipe any independence/multi-source findings INTO gradeConfidence. (Whether a reliable per-source publish date is parseable from Perplexity/Firecrawl at runtime is unverified — may degrade to 'unknown-age' for a fraction of sources; see gaps.)

findings.area: A4 — curated-layer flags bypass the gate and self-contradict (confirmed in-repo)
findings.finding: Curated country/category confidence values are hand-typed literals not run through demote(); confirmed this session that category-regime.ts:571-572 ship confidence:'single', citations:[] — directly violating the engine's own rule that single requires >=1 citation. This is a REAL in-repo contradiction, not a hypothesis. Best-practice literature converges on the same design: ground->verify-attribution post-hoc, classify per-claim, weight consensus by SOURCE INDEPENDENCE, prefer deterministic (auditable) over probabilistic.
findings.evidence: Verified category-regime.ts:571-572 (two routeClaims with confidence:'single', citations:[]) vs engine-light.ts:290 (citeCount===0->inferred); arXiv 2602.18693 / 2605.06635 'Cited but Not Verified' (cited as supporting literature — see gaps for residual-resolution status).
findings.implication: Add a build-time lint to the 5-gate asserting confidence==='single' => citations.length>=1 and confidence==='verified' => humanReviewed===true across the curated layer too — catches the EXISTING contradiction with no model in the loop. Split the single flag into 3 orthogonal predicates (URL resolves [deterministic]; source supports claim [entailment-scored, thresholded]; recency+independence [deterministic]); make the tooltip self-explaining ('1 independent source, published 2024').

findings.area: A5 — report blank/drop is a render-state seam, correctly hardened; keep the module latch as primary
findings.finding: The blank/jump (defect f / 2nd-recording P0) is an AUTOMATIC mechanism (TanStack-Query auto-refetch poll, route remount after gcTime, auto-skeleton early-returns) reverting a rendered report to skeleton. The data-state seam is correctly hardened via a module-level shownReports/lastGoodReports latch (load-bearing because placeholderData:(prev)=>prev is observer-level, never persisted to cache, and yields nothing on a true remount). The protection rests on a single everShown latch via a fragile 5-flag boolean.
findings.evidence: Verified report.$reportId.tsx:204-227 (module Set/Map + R136 comment) + downstream non-content returns; TanStack Query docs (placeholderData never persisted, lost after gc).
findings.implication: Keep the module shownReports Set + lastGoodReports Map as the PRIMARY cross-remount latch (placeholderData only as within-mount flicker guard); gate EVERY non-content return (progress/enriching, failed-job card, skeleton, error card) on everShown; add a regression test asserting once everShown, no skeleton/progress/error/failed return is reachable for any isLoading/isFetching/isError/enriching combination — turning the fragile boolean into a guaranteed invariant. NOTE: the _verify harness runs under jsdom in a separate copied env where the module-level Set persists across tests — RESET shownReports/lastGoodReports in beforeEach (or inject the latch) so the test proves the guarantee rather than inheriting prior-test state.

findings.area: A5 — two residual seams remain open, uncovered by the 5-gate, severity inferred-not-observed
findings.finding: (1) Scroll-restoration: router scrollRestoration:true + the ?fresh-strip navigate({replace}) restore a saved offset BEFORE the async report body reaches final height -> blank-at-fold or jump. (2) Cold JS realm: a hard reload inside the partitioned Lovable preview iframe wipes the per-realm module latch AND the localStorage/sessionStorage fallback no-ops in a partitioned iframe -> re-enters the cold path. The R136 comment correctly attributes the remount to gcTime eviction / genuine unmount / HMR (NOT the ?fresh-strip; search-param changes don't remount without remountDeps). Both residual seams are UNVERIFIED by any shipped fix note; the user-facing severity (fast skeleton vs multi-minute progress screen on a settled-report hard reload) has NOT been observed.
findings.evidence: Verified report.$reportId.tsx:204-227 (R136 comment names gcTime/remount/partitioned-iframe storage no-op); router scrollRestoration + TanStack remountDeps semantics (framework claims, needs runtime confirmation).
findings.implication: BEFORE sizing A5 remaining work, OBSERVE the actual behavior: hard-reload a settled report in the partitioned preview iframe and record what the user sees. Then: on the ?fresh-strip navigate call resetScroll/scroll-to-top and reserve a stable report min-height; keep the progress/enriching hold gated strictly on blockingResearch=pending||jobRunning (never on optional needsResearchPack/needsExecutiveUpgrade); add a headless test that scrolls a long settled report to the fold, triggers a poll settle + remount, and asserts no blank/jump. Re-scope A5 from 'the recorded blank' (verified fixed) to these two residual seams — do NOT mark DONE.

findings.area: Platform-fit 'Incumbent Gate' factor — real and stacking, but every dollar figure is a dated/ranged estimate, not a body-level fact
findings.finding: The default-placement 'gate pin contract' means 'install over native' starts from a structural disadvantage across THREE stacking moats: pre-install, prominent placement, default status. Marketplace analog = Buy Box / sponsored-slot self-preferencing. For CONQUER's consumer-goods scope the directly relevant analog is physical retail: slotting fees + category-captain control. Regulation erodes asymmetrically: the 2025 US v Google remedy bans EXCLUSIVE defaults but still permits PAY-for-default; EU DMA mandates easy uninstall + choice screens. CRITICAL CALIBRATION: the specific dollar figures (Google default-search spend, total partner payments, slotting cost/SKU, category-open %, browser-choice-screen selections) are litigation-era / unaudited industry ranges / an engagement-not-share metric — they must NOT appear as body-level point facts.
findings.evidence: US v Google (DOJ) trial + Sept 2025 remedy; UK CMA MADA/RSA appendices; Buy Box self-preferencing + FTC v Amazon; EU DMA Art.6(3). Dollar figures are reconstructed from confidential contracts / unaudited ranges (see gaps).
findings.implication: Add an explicit 'Incumbent Gate' factor: classify each channel as (a) contractually pinned [hard penalty], (b) pay-to-play but open, or (c) merit/algorithm-allocated; decompose the moat into the three stacking layers and report separately. For marketplaces, flag whether the platform runs a competing first-party/private-label line and whether prime placement is conditioned on its fulfillment. Use slotting cost/SKU/chain as the CONQUER-native consumer-goods entry-cost line item — modelled as a WIDE RANGE behind a dated, recency-flagged, runtime-curated tile with an explicit 'unaudited industry range' annotation, NEVER a point estimate. Make the factor jurisdiction-aware (EU choice-screen vs US pay-for-default) and qualify every gate finding with a switching-friction note ('technically allowed' != 'practically winnable').

findings.area: Cross-cutting invariant — trust signal is a recomputed pure function over the provenance object, never stored or self-reported
findings.finding: Every stream converges on one rule: the trust signal (A0 gate decision, A4 confidence flag) must be a deterministic function of evidence, recomputed at shaping/gate time, never a stored or model-emitted opinion — because models and humans both misremember provenance. CONQUER already enforces this for confidence (CHECK fabrication_law + BEFORE-INSERT trigger demoting checkmark->warn) and engine-light demotes 'regardless of what the model emitted'. The one honest exception: the 'source-supports-claim' sub-check is entailment-scored (probabilistic) gated by a deterministic threshold — not itself deterministic.
findings.evidence: engine-light.ts:281-292 (verified); CONQUER 03-claims.sql fabrication_law; arXiv 2509.11851 (AI Memory Gap — users misremember AI vs self-authored content; cited as supporting — see gaps for residual-resolution status).
findings.implication: Implement the deterministic parts of BOTH A0 and A4 (URL-resolves, hash/span-match, recency, independence clustering, count thresholds) as code/DB-constraint-level pure functions over the provenance object, applied uniformly to live AND curated layers with zero trusted inputs — so neither the judged agent nor a hand-typed literal can reintroduce the failure mode. Keep the entailment sub-check explicitly labelled as the one thresholded-probabilistic input.

designImplications: SPLIT THE ROADMAP. Track 1 (CONQUER, ship-now, user-pain-backed + code-verified): A3 (shared AbortController + signal-through-keyedFetch + replace the Promise.race leak), A4 (one gradeConfidence pure function over distinct-domains + real source-age, build-time single=>citations.length>=1 lint, checkmark-unreachable legend), A5 (keep module latch primary, close the two residual seams, invariant test with per-test latch reset). Track 2 (agent-safety R&D, gate behind 'observed in the wild' + a corpus pilot): A0, A1, A2. Do not let Track 2 block Track 1.

A0 — DE-CONFLATE into two deliverables in two runtimes. A0-runtime = extend engine-light demote() into a pure gradeConfidence() that grades the GENERATED REPORT (Cloudflare worker / SQL / _verify CI — mostly built). A0-agent = a Claude Code orchestrator/hook-level gate on what a subagent RETURNS (NOT built, NOT analogous to demote()). Name the enforcement locus per gate: pre-build = deterministic check on the returned provenance object; completion/'done' claim = a Stop/SubagentStop hook or orchestrator-side assertion (NO PreToolUse fires on a prose completion message); post-build = orchestrator-side re-resolve/span-match on the artifact bytes. Enumerate ALL Claude Code exit paths (Bash, Edit/Write/NotebookEdit, mcp__server__tool, final message) since 36.8% of state-changes bypassed via in-project edits in the stress test. State explicitly: no subagent grades another's hidden reasoning — only its returned artifact.

A0 — input contract = {source id + content hash + quote span}, independently re-resolved and span-matched; treat the agent's own deep-research URLs as untrusted (3-13% hallucinated, deep-research agents worst). Emit {ALLOW|BLOCK|ESCALATE} + a structured deny enum to the CONQUER incidents/audit ledger, computed from the provenance object never the model's verbalized confidence. Split by cost as a HARD constraint: cheap deterministic checks (URL-resolve, hash/span match) synchronous in the pre-gate; expensive checks (NLI/HHEM entailment, independence clustering) async in the post-gate or a sampled auditor — never inside the blocking hook window. Require a MEASURED end-to-end provenance-check latency on the tribunal's own corpus before locking thresholds; the cited 53ms/8.3% are from different mechanisms (policy-ACL / code-artifact) and are analogical priors, not the operating point.

A0 — fail-closed is a HYPOTHESIS, not a default. Gate by claim_class as a candidate: fail-closed (BLOCK/ESCALATE) for fabrication-prone classes, fail-open (demote-and-log, the CONQUER pattern) for static/low-stakes. Before flipping ANY class to fail-closed, run a pilot on the tribunal's OWN corpus, instrument block-rate + FPR from day one, and set the over-block alarm threshold first (over-blocking is a failure mode that breeds verification theater, especially for a single-user hands-off tool). Rename the 'source-supports-claim' predicate honestly to 'entailment-scored, thresholded' — keep only URL-resolves and recency/independence as truly deterministic.

A1 — build the delete-snapshot as a synchronous PreToolUse/Bash hook that triggers on destructive command SHAPES, copies resolved targets aside (reflink/hardlink/copy with a max-bytes cap), verifies the copy exists, THEN runs. DOWNGRADE-not-deadlock: on unresolvable/script-wrapped/glob targets escalate to 'ask' (never silent fail-open, never hard deny-all). Per-shell shape sets (POSIX rm/sed-i/find-delete/dd/git-reset-hard AND PowerShell Remove-Item/Clear-Content/Set-Content) and a Windows-viable snapshot (copy/VSS; reflink is ReFS/dev-drive-only on NTFS). MEASURE copy/reflink latency on the target FS before any 'cheap' claim. Surface 'NOT captured' classes to the user; never advertise 'fully reversible'. Cite GitHub #34368 (Windows-repro, deletion-undo that can't restore) as primary evidence. COW filesystem (YoloFS) is north-star v2.

A2 — PARK until need + feed schema are confirmed. Gate on: (a) a user actually wants an 'is this name paused?' flag AND a 60s-stale flag is useful given the halt mechanism moves ~4x faster; (b) one live Nasdaq Trade Halt RSS sample confirms the body field schema (resumption timestamp/reason vs HTML-only); (c) whether intraday halt state is needed at all vs an at-open snapshot (if at-open only, the 60s lag is largely moot). If built: poll exactly once/minute, stamp 'as of HH:MM:SS, up to 60s old', frame as contextual not real-time, never infer from 15-20min-delayed price feeds (label that delay separately), render resumption as 'expected ~5 min, pending auction + new bands', calibrate any open-time flag to the doubled 9:30-9:45 ET LULD bands, document the paid-feed ceiling. Consistent with the passive-only, no-runtime-cost constraint.

A3 — make the 'hard budget' real: thread a signal through every leaf (keyedFetch(service,path,payload,opts?:{signal}) using AbortSignal.any([controller.signal, opts.signal])), give runResearchBackbone ONE shared AbortController + aggregate budget (clearTimeout in finally), and replace verifyCompetitorEntities' leaky Promise.race([run(),setTimeout]) with an AbortController whose abort both wins the wait AND is handed to every verifyProduct fetch. Standardize on AbortSignal.any([parentSignal, AbortSignal.timeout(perCallMs)]) (workerd — runtime claim, confirm separately); do NOT rely on invocation-end float-cancel; optionally wire Request.signal so an abandoned report cancels paid research. Keep proportionate to Priority-4 — no p-limit/semaphore/task-runner; add one test asserting in-flight leaves are aborted when the budget fires.

A4 — make confidence ONE pure derived function gradeConfidence({validCitations, distinctDomains, sourceAgeMonths, isProjection}) routing BOTH the live engine and the curated layer, with zero trusted/stored inputs. Grade on DISTINCT DOMAINS not raw citation IDs (reuse the competitor domain-dedupe) to unlock a deterministically-earned middle rung with no Claude call. Stop stamping last_verified=today — parse a real per-source date and downgrade/annotate when the freshest source is >12-18mo (degrade gracefully to 'unknown-age' when no date is parseable). Keep checkmark structurally unreachable at runtime and SAY SO via a legend ('checkmark = human-reviewed'); make tooltips self-explaining ('1 independent source, published 2024').

A4 — add a build-time 5-gate lint asserting confidence==='single' => citations.length>=1 and confidence==='verified' => humanReviewed===true across the curated layer too — this catches the CONFIRMED in-repo contradiction (category-regime.ts:571-572 ship single + citations:[]) with no model in the loop. Structure the flag as 3 named/testable predicates: URL-resolves (deterministic), source-supports-claim (entailment-scored + deterministic threshold — labelled honestly), recency+independence (deterministic).

A5 — keep the module-level shownReports Set + lastGoodReports Map as the PRIMARY cross-remount latch (placeholderData:(prev)=>prev is only a within-mount flicker guard); gate EVERY non-content return on the single everShown latch and add a regression test asserting once everShown, no skeleton/progress/error/failed-card return is reachable for any isLoading/isFetching/isError/enriching combination — converting today's fragile 5-flag boolean into a guaranteed invariant. RESET the module latch in beforeEach (or inject it) so the jsdom _verify harness proves the guarantee rather than inheriting prior-test module state.

A5 — OBSERVE before sizing: hard-reload a settled report inside the partitioned preview iframe and record what the user actually sees (fast skeleton vs multi-minute progress). Then close the two residual seams: on the ?fresh-strip navigate({replace}) call resetScroll/scroll-to-top and reserve a stable report min-height so scrollRestoration:true can't restore against not-yet-rendered async content; keep the progress/enriching hold gated strictly on blockingResearch=pending||jobRunning; the R136 comment already correctly blames gcTime/unmount/HMR (not the ?fresh-strip); add a headless test that scrolls a long report to the fold, triggers a poll settle + remount, and asserts no blank/jump. Re-scope A5 from 'the recorded blank' (fixed) to these residual seams — do NOT mark DONE.

Platform-fit — add an explicit 'Incumbent Gate' factor: classify each channel as contractually-pinned (hard penalty) / pay-to-play-open / merit-allocated; decompose and report the incumbent moat as three stacking layers (pre-install, placement, default); for marketplaces flag whether the platform runs a competing first-party/private-label line and whether prime placement is conditioned on its fulfillment. Use slotting cost/SKU/chain as the CONQUER-native consumer-goods entry-cost line item — modelled as a WIDE RANGE behind a dated, recency-flagged, runtime-curated tile with an explicit 'unaudited industry range' annotation, NEVER a body-level point estimate (the Google/slotting/Mozilla dollar figures are litigation-era / unaudited / engagement-not-share). Make the factor jurisdiction-aware (EU mandated choice-screen/uninstall vs US pay-for-default) and qualify every gate finding with a switching-friction note ('technically allowed' != 'practically winnable').

Cross-cutting — implement the DETERMINISTIC parts of every trust signal (A0 gate decision, A4 confidence flag: URL-resolves, hash/span-match, recency, independence clustering, count thresholds) as recomputed pure functions over the provenance object at code/DB-constraint level, applied uniformly to live AND curated layers with zero trusted/self-reported inputs, mirroring the existing fabrication_law CHECK + BEFORE-INSERT trigger — so neither the judged agent nor a hand-typed literal can reintroduce the failure mode. Label the one entailment-based sub-check ('source supports claim') honestly as thresholded-probabilistic, not deterministic. Keep all fast-moving rule-sets (regulatory gate facts, source-age/freshness) runtime-curated and recency-flagged rather than hard-coded.
gaps: CITATION STATUS (resolved this session): arXiv 2511.05524 (EviBound), 2603.20953 (Before the Tool Call), 2604.03173 (reference hallucination), 2604.04978 (Measuring the Permission Gate), 2407.11843 (InferAct) all RESOLVE and confirm their KEPT core claims; the file-checkpointing doc and GitHub #34368 confirm verbatim. STILL UNRESOLVED (cited as supporting literature only, not load-bearing — verify before quoting any derived number): 2602.18693, 2605.06635 ('Cited but Not Verified'), 2509.11851 (AI Memory Gap), 2604.13536 (YoloFS/agent-filesystem). Treat any statistic from the unresolved set as inferred until its URL resolves and a span-match confirms support.

A0 — no published evaluation tests a provenance gate inside a self-critiquing 'tribunal' loop where the same model family both produces and partly judges the claim; the closest analogs gate code-execution artifacts (EviBound, n=8) or tool authorization, not free-text research claims. Generalization to the tribunal's exact use case is inferred, not measured. Fail-open vs fail-closed has no head-to-head benchmark on research-claim shipping with real over-blocking cost quantified; the over-block-cost evidence comes from the tool-authorization domain. The ~8.3% overhead and 53ms latency are real but measured on DIFFERENT mechanisms (code-artifact verify; cheap policy-ACL checks) — they are analogical priors, not A0's operating point.

A0 — latency/cost of the ACTUAL provenance checks the tribunal needs (URL resolution at scale, NLI/HHEM entailment, MinHash independence clustering) is unmeasured; whether a real-but-unsupporting URL passes a resolve-only gate is acknowledged (resolvability != support) but the residual rate after a span-match/entailment gate is unquantified. The 'source-supports-claim' check is irreducibly probabilistic (entailment), so it cannot be a fully deterministic predicate — only thresholdable.

A1 — no public benchmark exists for per-delete agent snapshot latency on the user's actual filesystem; reflink is not universally available on NTFS (ReFS/dev-drive only on Windows), so the Windows-first snapshot mechanism (copy/VSS) and its latency must be measured before any 'cheap' claim. Reliable path resolution for globs/recursion/variable-expansion and the script-wrapped bypass remain genuinely unsolved at the hook level — the design's answer is downgrade-to-ask, not full coverage.

A2 — UNCONFIRMED and gating: (a) whether the tool needs intraday halt state at all vs an at-open snapshot (if at-open only, the 60s lag is largely moot and the doubled-band calibration dominates); (b) the Nasdaq Trade Halt RSS body field schema (machine-readable resumption timestamp/reason/threshold vs HTML-only); (c) no measured end-to-end halt-to-feed lag (the 60s is a stated tier delay); (d) NYSE-direct halt-feed cadence/terms; (e) NO logged user request for the feature. A2 should be PARKED pending (a)+(b)+a user-need confirmation.

A4 — no written A4 spec was located in the repo; scope (extend demote vs new system) is inferred from code + the confidence-grammar skill + MEMORY. The engine path is a Cloudflare/Deno edge function not exercisable in the local 5-gate, so flag logic was verified by reading source, not by observing live emitted flags. Source-tiering (Tier A/B/C/D) is not represented in the engine data model — a deterministic tier classifier would need a maintained domain->tier registry whose presence/freshness in THIS repo is unconfirmed. Whether a reliable per-source publish date is parseable from Perplexity/Firecrawl results at runtime is unverified (may degrade to 'unknown-age' for a fraction of sources).

A5 — the two residual seams (cold-realm iframe reload, scroll-restoration jump) are unverified by any shipped fix note and uncovered by the 5-gate; severity is INFERRED, not observed. The exact behavior of a settled-report hard reload inside the partitioned preview iframe (fast skeleton vs multi-minute progress screen) must be observed before sizing the fix. The TanStack Router scrollRestoration/remountDeps and workerd AbortSignal claims (A3/A5) are framework/runtime assertions verified separately from the Claude Code primitives — keep them at 'needs runtime confirmation', distinct from the code-verified bugs.

Platform-fit — exact live 2026 MADA/RSA contract terms are confidential (reconstructed from CMA appendices + litigation); default-deal dollar figures are litigation-era (pre-Sept-2025-remedy renegotiations unconfirmed); the durable share-shift from a DMA choice screen is thinly evidenced (the cited browser-choice number is an engagement, not a share, metric); slotting/category-captain figures are unaudited industry ranges. None of these should appear as body-level point facts — model as wide, dated, recency-flagged ranges. The mapping of this antitrust/retail evidence onto CONQUER's live platform-fit schema is an analyst inference, not validated against the live engine.

SCOPE GAP — A0/A1/A2 have NO logged user incident behind them (papers + vendor docs only), unlike A3/A4/A5 which trace to conquer_recording_defects.md. Before building any Track-2 item, attach a real trigger (logged incident, user complaint, or concrete near-miss); absent one, treat the item as speculative backlog, not a defect. Open question whether the single hands-off end user reads/trusts confidence flags at all — if the legend/tooltips go unnoticed, prioritize verdict-line honesty (A4 'verified today' on stale sources) over the deeper gate plumbing.
